exposure: Fetal pelvic index cut-off value of -0.65
cohort: Pregnant women who underwent X-ray or MRI pelvimetry due to increased risk of cephalopelvic disproportion at North Karelia Central Hospital from 2000-2008
finding: The fetal pelvic index was not a clinically useful predictor of cesarean section for patients at high risk of cephalopelvic disproportion.
mod_finding: The study examined the use of the fetal pelvic index to predict cesarean section due to cephalopelvic disproportion but did not compare different modes of delivery beyond this.
